visualization.histogram: Select if the distribution is approximately symmetric and skewness is low.
visualization.box plot: Select if outliers or moderate to high skewness are detected.
visualization.density plot: Select if the sample size is large and smooth distribution estimation is required.
visualization.violin plot: Select if multimodal distribution or outliers are detected, combining density and spread.
visualization.Q-Q plot: Select if skewness and kurtosis suggest checking normality visually.

selection_criteria: Step 1: Perform Shapiro-Wilk test first to assess normality.
Step 2: If Shapiro-Wilk p-value > 0.05, proceed with one-sample t-test or z-test based on sample size and known/unknown population variance.
Step 3: If Shapiro-Wilk p-value <= 0.05, data is not normal. Consider non-parametric alternatives if available.
Step 4: Confidence intervals can be used regardless of normality but interpret cautiously if the distribution is highly skewed.

visualization.bar chart: Select to display frequency of each discrete value clearly.
visualization.histogram: Select to show distribution pattern of discrete values when many unique values exist.
visualization.dot plot: Select for simple display of individual data points when sample size is small.

selection_criteria: Step 1: Determine if testing mean against known value or testing distribution pattern.
Step 2: Use one-sample t-test for testing mean of discrete variable against known value.
Step 3: Use chi-square goodness of fit if testing whether data follows expected discrete distribution.
Step 4: Use Poisson test specifically for count data to test if it follows Poisson distribution.

visualization.bar chart: Select to compare frequencies across categories effectively.
visualization.pie chart: Select to show proportional breakdown when number of categories is small (<=5).
visualization.frequency table: Select for tabular display of counts and percentages.

selection_criteria: Step 1: Use chi-square goodness of fit if testing whether observed proportions match expected proportions across multiple categories.
Step 2: Use binomial test specifically for binary outcomes when testing a single proportion.
Step 3: Ensure expected frequencies are >5 for chi-square test validity.

visualization.bar chart: Select to display ordered categories while maintaining sequence.
visualization.ordered bar chart: Select to emphasize the natural ordering of categories.

selection_criteria: Step 1: Use Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to assess if data follows expected distribution pattern.
Step 2: Use runs test to check for randomness in the ordered sequence.
Step 3: Ensure sufficient sample size for meaningful results.
